preamble: The close-mid back rounded vowel [o] is realized as the unrounded [ʌ] under vowel reduction. The best-known case is Russian akanye: unstressed /o/ after a hard consonant in the syllable immediately before the stress (and word-initially) merges with /a/. Yanushevskaya & Bunčić (2015) describe this first-degree reduced vowel as [ʌ] in St Petersburg pronunciation and [ɐ] in Moscow pronunciation, and their St Petersburg speaker has года [ɡʌˈd̪aˑ] 'years' beside stressed год 'year'. Further from the stress the same /o/ reduces to [ə].

languageExamples.context: First pretonic syllable and word-initial position, after hard consonants

examples.from: говорить 'to speak', /o/ in the syllable before the stress
examples.note: Narrow transcription of a St Petersburg speaker (Yanushevskaya & Bunčić 2015): the /o/ immediately before the stress is [ʌ], the /o/ further from it [ə].

examples.from: года 'years', /o/ in the syllable before the stress (cf. stressed год 'year')
examples.note: Narrow transcription of the same St Petersburg speaker (Yanushevskaya & Bunčić 2015).

examples.from: города 'cities', /o/ in the syllable before the stress (cf. stressed город 'city')
examples.note: Yanushevskaya & Bunčić (2015): the /o/ immediately before the stress is [ʌ], the /o/ two syllables before it [ə̝].

sources: Yanushevskaya, I., & Bunčić, D. (2015). Russian. Journal of the International Phonetic Association 45(2), 221–228. https://doi.org/10.1017/S0025100314000395
